messages:
nora_support: ACME reporting sudden p95/p99 tail increase in us-west-2 after nightly maintenance. p95 ~200ms -> 800ms, p99 ~120ms -> 1.2s on /v1/embeddings and chat.generate. No 5xxs, just long tails. Started ~2026-03-12T02:15Z. Trace sample: trc_98321 req=acme-req-45. Attaching short logs and a small flame from spans.
jamie_ops: Can you paste node/pod ids and the kernel/driver versions? Also any recent CUDA/firmware rollouts in that window?
 nora_support: Customer sent these request IDs and sample traces. Affected request IDs: acme-req-45, acme-req-82, acme-req-97. From our side acme traffic concentrated on node-uw2-03 / pod redwood-kv-45 and node-uw2-07 / redwood-gen-12.
samir_eng: Quick findings from nodes: host kernel 6.2.14-rc deployed in maintenance window, NVIDIA driver 535.54 pushed to uw2 cluster at 02:00Z, GPU firmware 86.3. NVMe stats show qdepth spikes (nvme0): 4k rq/s bursts and svctm tailing. kvcache eviction rate spiked x8.
li_yang: iostat snapshot (abridged):
  Device            r/s     w/s    rkB/s    wkB/s   await  svctm  %util
  nvme0n1         2000    900   51200    20480   18.9   1.2   95.4
Also host writeback CPU up ~30%, dmesg has repeated block layer timeouts on nvme0 (throttle messages).
maria_sre: Not seeing HTTP error budget hits, this is pure tail latency. Likely host-level IO interference causing process scheduling delays and kv-cache thrashing.
jamie_ops: Repro steps for infra team: 1) run `iostat -x 1 5` on affected nodes; 2) `cat /sys/module/nvme/parameters/q_depth` and check firmware versions `nvme id-ctrl /dev/nvme0`; 3) capture `perf top`/`pidstat` while running a small synthetic embedding workload.
samir_eng: I ran a small repro locally against the same node image with the new driver and saw similar tail. Using the prior driver (525.85) the tails disappear. Hypothesis: driver+firmware combo changes IO scheduling behavior that amplifies hostfs write bursts -> heavy KV cache eviction -> long GLIBC wakeups in the inference process.
li_yang: Also noticed kernel page reclaim spikes after heavy kvcache flushes. Kernel 6.2.14-rc introduced a pagecache heuristic change that seems to correlate.
maria_sre: Immediate mitigations: 1) move ACME traffic to dedicated-gpu-pool-1 (isolated NVMe). 2) throttle background host IO via cgroups blkio/IOQoS on affected nodes. 3) temporary model throttling: route to smaller embedding model with less KV working set.
jamie_ops: I'll prepare a canary rollback of the NVIDIA driver on two nodes (node-uw2-03, node-uw2-07) to 525.85 and drain kvcache, then re-run the synthetic load. Plan: rollback + restart inference service on canary nodes, monitor p95/p99, then expand rollback if good.
deploy-bot: Deploy plan: rollback-driver job queued for node-uw2-03,node-uw2-07. ETA 15m. Will annotate runbook.
nora_support: Notified ACME that we're investigating and will fail them over to dedicated pool to reduce impact. They asked for ETA to normal service.
samir_eng: After driver rollback on node-uw2-03 we saw p99 drop from 1.15s -> 210ms within 3 minutes. kvcache eviction rate returned to baseline. nvme0 util dropped to ~40%.
li_yang: Applying blkio cgroup limits to other hosts to reduce noisy background flushes. Also applying a kernel backport patch to tweak pagecache reclaim heuristic on the staging cluster for further testing.
maria_sre: Action items: - jamie_ops to run broader rollback plan if canary stays green (owner: jamie_ops) - samir_eng to create an eval to detect this pattern (kv eviction + nvme qdepth) and alert (owner: samir_eng) - li_yang to document IO throttles + recommended cgroup settings (owner: li_yang) - nora_support to confirm ACME is back to acceptable SLOs and provide customer postmortem (owner: nora_support).
jamie_ops: Canary green after 20m, expanding rollback to 6 nodes in us-west-2 and routing ACME back from dedicated pool gradually. Monitoring dashboard: p95/p99 trending down. :thumbsup:
nora_support: Customer confirmed baseline restored, p95/p99 back within SLOs. Will schedule postmortem with timeline and recommendations (driver gating, firmware canary, IO isolation defaults). Thanks team. :white_check_mark:
